paper.paper_scope: Effects of alloy composition (Mn/Ni ratio), 50% cold rolling and subsequent heat treatment temperature (873–1173 K) on concurrent κ-carbide/B2 precipitation and austenite recrystallization, and the resulting hardness and tensile properties, in three Fe-Mn-Al-C-(Ni) austenitic low-density steels (28Mn0Ni, 28Mn5Ni, 15Mn5Ni).
paper.title: Effect of cold rolling and subsequent heat treatment on microstructural evolution and mechanical properties of Fe-Mn-Al-C-(Ni) based austenitic low-density steels

processes.description: 30 kg ingot homogenized at 1423 K for 2.5 h and then hot rolled at 1323 K to a final plate thickness of ~13 mm; referred to as HR.
processes.processes_notes: Baseline state common to all three alloys; HR microstructures were reported in a previous study [21] and are used as the starting condition for cold rolling.

processes.description: Hot rolled plate cold rolled at room temperature in several passes to ~50% reduction in thickness (~6 mm sheets); denoted HR+CR. Reduction capped at 50% for all alloys since 15Mn5Ni cracked beyond 50%.
processes.processes_notes: Applied to all three alloys for a common degree of cold work to allow comparison.

source.reason: Block b0015 states samples were cold rolled to ~50% reduction in thickness at room temperature and denoted HR+CR; block b0070 explains the 50% restriction.

unmapped_findings: The microstructures and mechanical properties of the three alloys in the hot rolled (HR) condition were reported in the authors' previous study [21]; the present work focuses on cold rolling and subsequent heat treatment.

Inconsistency in reported heat-treatment temperature: block b0062 mentions 15Mn5Ni specimens heat treated at 1073 K showing negligible ductility, whereas other sections (block b0051, Table 3) refer to 1023 K for the same conditions.

Tensile properties of 15Mn5Ni alloy heat treated at 973 K and 1023 K are not available because the alloy exhibited brittle behavior (total elongation <1%) and stress-strain curves could not be recorded.

Reported B2 particle composition by TEM-EDS (Table 2/b0053-b0054): in 28Mn5Ni at 973 K Mn 16.3/Al 12.7/Ni 24.6 wt.%; at 1173 K Ni increased to 26.1-27.5 wt.%; in 15Mn5Ni at 1173 K Mn 8.7-10.5/Al 12.8-13.5/Ni 20.2-22.0 wt.%, with Fe balance.
κ-carbide sizes: 10-60 nm in deformed austenite; intragranular B2 5-20 nm (TEM) / 50-200 nm (SEM); intergranular B2 50-200 nm / 0.5-1.5 μm depending on characterization scale.
B2 volume fraction in 15Mn5Ni decreased from ~40% to ~15% as heat treatment temperature increased from 973 K to 1173 K; prior B2 fraction in HR condition ~12% for 15Mn5Ni and ~4% for 28Mn5Ni.
